text: An agent is a role and not a second mechanism: the agent roles are the roles whose role_class is the non-human actor class of LOV-ROLE-CLASS, the matrix covers them with the same fourteen capability areas and the same five letters as a person role, and the five system roles of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-OCR, SY-AGENT) are those roles. An agent grant carries, in addition to the letters, the reference of the agent's service identity (agentRef), which is required on a non-human actor role and refused 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming agentRef where it is missing; the identity itself and the allowed-action list of an agent stay with rwb-agent (P10) and are not read here. The matrix surface is composed at the edge by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and the four operations are GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles (API-P4-007), GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/agents, PUT /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles/{roleCode}/permissions and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-matrix.
why: The legacy story says each role and each agent, and no source gives this service an agent table, an identity column or an agent screen: the field catalog of FSD P4 v3 A2.30 names a role class with a non-human actor value, the technical specification lists five system roles in the matrix, and the ownership rows give P4 five tables none of which holds an identity. Without this ruling the agent half would either be dropped or become a second grant mechanism with a second shape, and a non-human actor could read more than its letters allow.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-019 (story statement, AC1, data rows role and v_ace_iam_group, screens SCR-39 and SCR-41); FSD P4 v3 A2.30.1 to A2.30.3.3; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (role, permission), T3.2 (the lists), T6.1 (the matrix with the five system roles) and T6.2; NFR-051 and REQ-ACA-010; the context pack rows for P4 (five tables, four provided operations, no event); DP-05 and DP-19; Template and Rules R5.7 Day-1 rule.
confirm: Solution architect with the tech lead of rwb-access and the owner of the agent platform at the matrix design review
impact: If the agent's identity must be held in a table of its own, the ownership map gains a table, the Flyway story of this service changes and the grant carries a key rather than a reference; the letters, the areas, the four paths and the report do not change.

text: The matrix paths are authorised by the Platform administration letters of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and API-P4-007: R on the roles read, the agents read and the report, and C on the grant write, held by RW-SECADM as CRUDA, RW-PLATADM as CRUD, RW-COMPLY, RW-CONDUCT, RW-DATASTEW and RW-AUDIT as R, and RW-COE as R only. The legacy permission table of RWB-E8-019, which gives Rules and parameters C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK, is the rule-change right set of the same chapter and not this feature's; R-PREC puts the Technical Specifications above the story master. A caller without the letter is refused 403 with MSG-P4-002, and a caller with no session is 401 with MSG-P4-001.
why: Three sources disagree on who may set access: the legacy table names Rules and parameters letters that belong to the rule-change journey, the FSD names the security administrator as the primary role of the feature, and the technical specification, which outranks the story master, gives RW-SECADM CRUDA and RW-COE R in Platform administration; a story that kept the legacy letters would let the center of excellence change access while the security administrator's own feature contradicted it.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-019 permission checks; FSD P4 v3 A2.30.3.3 roles and permissions; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 RBAC matrix and T6.2; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A API-P4-007 (Platform administration R); Template and Rules R3 R-PREC; MSG-P4-001 and MSG-P4-002 in the legacy message table.
confirm: Solution architect with the owner of the permission matrix and the security administrator at the P4 design review
impact: If the matrix is later changed, only the permission rows and the SIT users of the tests change and no code does; if the legacy letters were kept instead, RW-COE could set access and the security administrator's own feature would contradict the matrix.

text: The rule version of legacy AC1 is the matrix version of this feature, read from permission.matrix_version (DF-REF-044) in force on the date of the set; a set mints the next label (the sample of SIT is PM-2026.11 in force and PM-2026.12 after the set), stamps the changed rows with it and supersedes the version in force, and no letter is changed in place. Every set writes one entry of the local decision-record chain of DP-03 under the access-change code of the library, carrying the role code, the role class, the capability area, the letters before and after, both matrix versions, the parameters version in force and the agent reference, hash-linked and in the same transaction as its idempotency and outbox rows. The central ledger decision_log_entry stays in rwb-decision and is never read or written here. The code and the field-level shape of the entry, and the version label format beyond the sample, are settled with the ledger owner before the baseline is tagged.
why: The legacy criterion requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version, the sources give a version column and no code, and the monolith stamped nothing: without this ruling the criterion cannot be tested, and an in-place edit would destroy the only evidence of which letters were in force on a date.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-019 AC1 and AC2; FSD P4 v3 A2.30.4.1 and A2.30.4.3; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-044 matrix_version) and T6.3 (a change entry is append only, with the version label, the status change, the author and the time); Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 DF-DEC-003 and DF-DEC-008; DP-03; R-UNI-38 and R-UNI-39.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-access with the owner of the decision-record library, the owner of the matrix load story and the Internal audit representative
impact: A different code, a different placement of the letters or a different label format changes the value written on every entry and the filter audit uses; the four paths, the closed sets and the report columns do not change.

text: The count of Entra ID groups mapped to a role and the date of that data are read from the read-only view v_ace_iam_group under the DP-05 boundary and are shown as two report columns (aceGroupCount and aceDataAsOf); the column role.entra_group of TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-039) is not written by this story and no group membership is copied into a table of rwb-access. A role with no row in the view is reported with a count of zero and the data_as_of of the view.
why: The technical specification carries the group as a column of the role table while the functional specification states that it is read from ACE and is not a Workbench column, and the ownership rows give this service no group table; copying membership into rwb_access would create a second, stale copy of an Entra ID decision that ACE Common owns.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.30.3.2 (v_ace_iam_group.entra_group read from ACE, iam_group, not a Workbench column); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-039 entra_group, source Entra ID); TSD P4 v3 T3.2; Legacy RWB-E8-019 data rows DF-ACE-301 to DF-ACE-304; DP-05; Template and Rules R3 R-PREC.
confirm: Data steward with the owner of the ACE group feed and the tech lead of rwb-access at the matrix design review
impact: If the group must be held as a column, the sync from ACE becomes a scheduled job of this service with its own story and the report reads the column; the letters, the paths and the count column do not change.

text: This story publishes the decision-record message rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1 and no message on rwb.access.events.v1: a grant is announced on the service's one access-policy name rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 by the matrix-version approval path of RWB-P4-E1037-APP, with its own change kind, because this story's pattern set and build dependencies carry the decision-record library (DP-03) and not the outbox platform story (DP-09). The services that cache permission data refresh on that name and resolve the matrix version in force on each check through the guard contract RWB-P4-E1037-CON, so an answer cached before a set is never mixed with an answer after it.
why: The legacy criterion asks only for the decision-log write, the architecture gives the service one access-policy name and one delegation name, and no source gives a single grant an event of its own; declaring a second name here would add a contract without a consumer and a dependency this story does not carry.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-019 AC1 and AC2; Architecture v5 slides 14, 20 and 41 to 43 (rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1, cache refresh on the policy event); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03 and DP-09 and R5.7; RWB-P4-AD002-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON (the load path and its event).
confirm: Solution architect with the owner of the matrix load path and the owner of the Kafka platform story at the contract review
impact: If a grant must announce on its own, the story gains RWB-PLT-TE006-CON as a build dependency and a second declaration with a change kind of its own; the paths, the schemas, the record and the report do not change.
